caption: 1 · The twelve base themes (the person, 2026-11-22), Sage the default; each is paper, ink and one accent; marks and folder colors stay yours
2 · The twelve in dark: each keeps its accent, lifted for a dark page
3 · Page surface: Paper, Sepia, Night or your own colors, for the reader and pages only; the theme stays
4 · Scripture faces side by side at reading size (all free and open licensed); Crimson Pro is the fifth, drawn on request
5 · Reading: no rail, no chrome but a quiet top line; the dock waits at the bottom edge
6 · The dock up: home, the apps, Settings; open apps carry a dot; the name shows on hover
7 · A click on Notebook opens it on this desk beside what is there (or brings it forward); the dock sinks as the pointer leaves
8 · Right-click an app in the dock: its recent items, New window, Keep in dock or Remove
9 · Static taskbar (Settings › Dock › Always shown): the same apps, always visible, the reader stops above it
10 · Settings › Dock: on hover or always shown, the edge (bottom by default; here left, as it would look), growing on hover, the apps' order
11 · The Workbench home: where you left off, today's reading, open questions, recent pages; one click resumes each
12 · Continue reading: the Bible at the verse you left, lit briefly; back returns to the Workbench
13 · Together A, Snap: drag an app's title to the top edge for layouts (halves, two-thirds, thirds, quarters); like Windows snap layouts
14 · Together B, Stage: the working set in the middle; other sets wait at the left as small cards, one click swaps them in (like Stage Manager)
15 · Together C, Desks: a named, saved arrangement of apps per task; switching desks swaps the whole screen; nothing stays open unseen
16 · Keys: holding Ctrl shows each app's number on the dock
17 · Drag a bubble by its title: it lifts and follows the pointer, a little larger, with a deeper shadow
18 · Magnetic: near another bubble's edge a soft outline shows where it will sit beside; let go and it pulls in
19 · Dropped onto another bubble (not its edge) the outline wraps it: let go and the two stack
20 · Always tiled: bubbles never overlap; every drop reflows the desk into columns
21 · Free canvas: bubbles float and may overlap; only a drop on a title stacks, only the top edge snaps
22 · Dragged to the top edge: the layouts appear (halves, two-thirds, thirds, quarters); the cell under the pointer lights
23 · Dropped on a layout cell: the bubble takes it, the desk's other bubbles fill the other cells, any extra stack on the last
24 · Dragged onto a desk's name: the name is outlined; let go and the bubble moves to that desk
25 · A stack rests as fanned cards: the edges of the ones behind show up and to the right; its title says how many
26 · Click a card behind: it comes to the front of its stack
27 · ⤫ takes a bubble out of its stack; it finds room beside
28 · Phone: a stack is one card with dots under it; swipe sideways through the desk's cards
29 · Each its own bubble: three passages open as three bubbles, tinted alike; a word opened from each sits beside it
30 · One app, many inside: a second and third passage open as columns inside the Bible bubble already there
31 · Both: each opens as a bubble; ⇲ on one gathers the app's bubbles into it as columns
32 · ⇱ pop out: a column leaves the bubble and becomes its own, beside it
33 · Following a word, linked: it opens beside the passage with a thread showing what led where
34 · Replace in place: the same bubble becomes the word; ← goes back to the passage (Alt+click does this in any mode)
35 · Ask each time: a small choice where the word goes: here, beside, or on a new desk
36 · A rabbit hole: passage → word → another verse that uses it, opened lit at that verse; the threads trace the path
37 · History of this desk, as a scrubber: every step on a line from earlier to now, with what it was and when
38 · Dragging the scrubber back replays the desk live, tinted slightly to show it is the past
39 · Let go and act in the past: a new branch begins; the later steps are kept, not lost
40 · The map: each step a dot; a second lane is the branch where you went back and took another way; click a dot to go there
41 · ◷ on a bubble: the history of that bubble only (the passages and words it showed)
42 · The whole app: every desk's steps on one line, switching desks included
43 · Your writing goes back with the desk: scrubbing before an edit shows the page as it was then
44 · Ctrl+Z outside a page steps the desk back one step (inside a page it undoes typing)
45 · Phone: each bubble is a full card; desks along the top; swipe between cards
46 · Phone: the dock is always shown at the bottom; a word opens as the next card
47 · + New desk: an empty desk named for now, renamed by double-click; open apps from the dock onto it
48 · Click a desk: the whole screen becomes that desk, its bubbles where they were
49 · The Workbench (home) from the dock: where you left off, today's reading, an open question, every desk
50 · The dock rises when the pointer reaches the bottom edge; a dot under each app open on this desk
